Slope Plot Type

Source: R/type_slope.R
type_slope.Rd

Creates publication-ready slope plots (slopegraphs) showing how paired values change between two or more conditions. Ideal for before/after treatment comparisons and paired time-course data. Inspired by cnsplots' slopeplot().

Usage

type_slope(
  pair = NULL,
  color_by = NULL,
  linewidth = 0.65,
  point_size = 2.6,
  line_alpha = 0.65,
  point_alpha = 0.9,
  reorder_x = TRUE
)

Arguments

pair

Column name (or vector) identifying paired observations. Lines connect the same subject across conditions.

color_by

Optional column name used to color the paired lines (e.g. responder status). Defaults to the by grouping variable.

linewidth

Width of the connecting lines (default 0.65).

point_size

Size of the points (default 2.6).

line_alpha

Transparency of the lines (default 0.65).

point_alpha

Transparency of the points (default 0.9).

reorder_x

Reorder the x-axis categories in order of appearance (default TRUE).

Value

A cliplot_type object for use with cliplot.

Details

Use the formula interface cliplot(value ~ condition, data, type = "slope") with type_slope(pair = "subject") to draw one line per paired subject across conditions. The optional color_by column highlights groups (e.g. responders vs non-responders).

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
cliplot(value ~ timepoint, data = paired_df,
        type = type_slope(pair = "patient", color_by = "responder"))
} # }
